clue.text: Pub pickings a big disappointment for many Labour politicians recently

definitions.text: a big disappointment for many Labour politicians recently

parts.note: a local is the pub nearest one's home, the one a person regularly drinks in
elections are choosings, so pickings in the sense of selections

explanation.surface: Bar snacks somehow stand for a political letdown, as if Labour MPs were grumbling about the crisps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pub pickings' looks like bar nibbles; it is two separate words, a British pub called a local plus pickings as choices.
explanation.definitionFit: Council polls in which Labour fared badly were a letdown for the party when the puzzle appeared.

clue.text: In the past they' ve ousted tenants — for a Scottish equivalent of a cricket ground?

definitions.text: In the past they' ve ousted tenants

indicators.note: a Scot says laird for lord, so the vowel of the ground's name is swapped for the Scottish one

parts.note: Lord's in London is the most famous cricket ground

explanation.surface: A question about what the Scots would call their version of a famous cricket venue, with an aside about evictions.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highland Clearances saw Scottish landowners evict their crofting tenants in the 18th and 19th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Lairds are Scottish landed proprietors, notorious for the clearances that drove tenants off estates.

clue.text: Star briefly rises in Wycomb election

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top
the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the town's name and the next word

explanation.surface: A political star makes a showing in a High Wycombe poll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' belongs to the definition, signalling a shortened form of the word for a famous person.
explanation.definitionFit: Celeb is the clipped informal form of celebrity, a famous person or star.

clue.text: His organ keeps many entertained ~ God, what a small specimen!

parts.note: the Lord is a name for God
a gnome is a tiny folklore figure, so a small example of a person

explanation.surface: Someone's organ gives pleasure to many, followed by a dismissive remark about its owner's size.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Gnome is Private Eye's mythical proprietor; the organ is the magazine, a newspaper being an organ, not a body part as the smutty surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional owner of the satirical magazine is the man whose publication amuses its many readers.

clue.text: Technophobe did cartwheels inside instrument

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed within the instrument

parts.note: a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

indicators.note: something turning cartwheels is tumbling over, so the letters of did are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone afraid of technology tumbles about inside a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Luddites were machine-breakers of the early 1800s, and the word now means anyone hostile to new technology.

clue.text: Delirious etc, about arse of highly fanciable type

indicators.note: the mixed letters go around the bottom
a delirious mind is scrambled, so the letters of etc are mixed up

parts.note: the rump is the buttocks

explanation.surface: A frenzied comment about the backside of someone very attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: Crumpet is British slang for sexually attractive people; it is also a griddle cake.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang crumpet means a desirable person, viewed as an object of lust.

clue.text: A rock in the main, kinky Les is into sex

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for sex

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal or sex itself

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the name's letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A seaside rock, and a man called Les with unusual sexual tastes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic word for the open sea; 'is into' looks like enthusiasm but places one piece within another.
explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a very small island, such as a rock standing out in the sea.

clue.text: Piss yourself

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the nursery euphemism for urinating
second meaning: looking after oneself is looking after this

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as a crude instruction to wet oneself; they are separate meanings of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Children call a wee this, and the idiom 'look after number one' means look after oneself.

clue.text: Without vitality, piss-poor Times shows undue self-regard

indicators.note: here meaning outside: the jumbled letters sit outside the energy word
a very poor version of the word is a mangled one, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A lifeless, dreadful edition of The Times reveals an excess of self-importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but has its old sense of 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotism is an excessive sense of one's own importance, an inflated vanity.

clue.text: Bill getting screwed — bloody loutish

indicators.note: screwed means twisted round, so these letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: blood is red, so bloody gives the colour

explanation.surface: A man named Bill being cheated, and a rough, swearing yob.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with bad manners and poor upbringing behaves like a lout, coarsely and rudely.

clue.text: Glum guy's scruffy and a terrible kisser

indicators.note: something scruffy is messy and dishevelled, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A morose, unkempt man who is bad at kissing.
explanation.walkthrough: Kisser is slang for face, not someone who kisses; the 's after guy stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly mug is an unattractive face, and kisser is informal for the face or mouth.

clue.text: Flipping have sex with Silver — get pants off!

indicators.note: flipped over, the word is read backwards

parts.note: to bed someone is to have sex with them
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An exasperated urge to sleep with someone called Silver and strip off.
explanation.walkthrough: Debagging is an old British student prank of pulling someone's trousers off; 'pants' here means trousers, as in American usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To debag a person is to remove their trousers forcibly, usually as a joke.

clue.text: A favoured NHS client? As a bed-occupier, probably not!

definitions.text: A favoured NHS client? As a bed-occupier, probably not!

parts.words: A favoured NHS client? As a bed-occupier, probably not
parts.note: split as the enumeration shows, the answer is what a model, uncomplaining patient would say; read as one word, it is how a bed-bound hospital in-patient probably feels

explanation.surface: A wry dig at the National Health Service, Britain's public health system, and its waiting patients.
explanation.walkthrough: The enumeration (2,7) splits the word into a self-description; read whole it means restless, which is how a bed-bound patient probably feels.
explanation.definitionFit: The ideal health-service user declares calm tolerance of waiting, while the joined word means the opposite: restless.

clue.text: Somehow gets balls stuck inside butt

indicators.note: the round letters are placed within the jumbled ones
somehow implies the letters arrive in some unspecified rearranged way

parts.note: two balls look like two round letters

explanation.surface: A crude image of balls being lodged in a bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: Butt here means the target of jokes, not the backside the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A stooge is a person made the object of ridicule or used as a foil, like the butt of jokes.

clue.text: Neat, these bent politicians gathered abroad

indicators.note: bent means corrupt in British slang and also twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tidy-looking but corrupt politicians meeting overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' reads as crooked politicians; it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Senate is the upper legislative chamber in America and elsewhere, an assembly of foreign lawmakers.

clue.text: Teletubbie surrounded by nipples and drink containers

indicators.note: the character sits inside the nipples word

parts.note: teats are nipples, of an animal or a feeding bottle
Po is the small red character in the children's TV show Teletubbies

explanation.surface: A children's TV character encircled by nipples, and some vessels for drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Teapots are vessels for brewing and pouring tea, a drink.

clue.text: Upset at Tories stifling Left's man of ideas

indicators.note: the jumbled letters smother the single letter by surrounding it
upset means knocked over, so these letters are tipped into a new order

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Annoyed Conservatives suppressing a left-wing thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Left's is link material between the indicator and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the Greek philosopher, the archetypal thinker whose work rests on ideas.

clue.text: The sound of a sudden involuntary ejaculation can be — is — a hoot

definitions.text: The sound of a sudden involuntary ejaculation

indicators.note: the letters can be made into the answer, that is, rearranged into it

explanation.surface: A smutty claim that an unplanned emission is hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: Ejaculation here is a sudden exclamation or expulsion of breath, a sneeze, not the sexual sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Atishoo is the British spelling of the noise of a sneeze, a sudden reflex expulsion of air.

clue.text: Auntie Beth rudely hogs the buzzer

indicators.note: to hog something is to keep it to oneself, so the jumbled name holds the buzzer inside
done rudely, roughly, the name's letters are knocked about

parts.note: a bee buzzes

explanation.surface: A relative called Beth selfishly keeps the doorbell to herself.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie and the Beeb are both affectionate British nicknames for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's national broadcaster is nicknamed both Auntie and the Beeb.

clue.text: "Victoria's mate to live with drunken hack, Mirror's chief"

parts.note: to be is to exist

indicators.note: a drunken word staggers, so its letters lurch into a new order
the chief letter is the first one

parts.note: the first letter of the newspaper's name, the Daily Mirror being a British tabloid

explanation.surface: A tabloid snippet: a Victoria moving in with a drunk reporter and a newspaper's boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria Beckham, the former Spice Girl, is married to the footballer David.
explanation.definitionFit: The England footballer is the husband, or partner, of Victoria the singer and designer.

clue.text: Carrots give Brown one form of BSE

parts.note: br is the standard abbreviation for brown
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: a form of something is one version of it, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A redhead offers Gordon Brown a strain of mad cow disease.
explanation.walkthrough: BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease; carrots here are inducements, as in carrot and stick, not a redhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Inducements offered to influence someone, like carrots dangled before a donkey, are corrupt payments.

clue.text: Prime Minister, not much up top, needs a victory

parts.note: a person with little hair on the head
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A dim-witted premier who needs a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not much up top' suggests stupidity but means hairless. Stanley Baldwin was a Conservative Prime Minister three times between the wars.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Baldwin led the British government in the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Pet the area between waist and knees, follow?

parts.words: the area between waist and knees
parts.note: the lap is the flat area formed by the thighs when seated
to dog someone is to follow them closely

explanation.surface: An instruction to stroke someone's lap, then trail after them.
explanation.walkthrough: Pet reads as a verb in the surface; it is the noun for a companion animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapdog is a small pet dog, also used of a servile follower.

clue.text: Non-believers are getting church in plastic construction

definitions.note: an adjective clause: what doubters are, matching the adjectival answer

indicators.note: the church letters are set within the rebuilt plastic, as a thing sits in a container
a construction is a building up of something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Atheists taking over a church made of plastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubters and atheists are inclined to question claims, which is to be doubtful by nature.

clue.text: Judge, irksome type

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who tries a case in court
second meaning: someone who tries your patience

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses come from the verb try: to hear a case, or to test someone's patience.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names one who tries, whether a legal case or another person's patience.

clue.text: Group of Pacific islands in Washington gaffe

indicators.note: the letters run inside the words that follow, across the gap between them

parts.note: the islands' name spans the end of the city and the start of the blunder

explanation.surface: A diplomatic blunder in the American capital involving a South Seas nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Polynesian kingdom spread over an archipelago in the southern Pacific.

clue.text: One bitch on the up as a super-model

indicators.note: in a down entry this means the letters are written upwards

parts.note: to bitch is to complain, to moan

explanation.surface: A single nasty woman rising to the top as a fashion icon.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitch is the verb meaning grumble; Naomi Campbell is the British supermodel.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi Campbell is a famous fashion model, so her first name stands for a top model.

clue.text: Airline in Idaho upset prophet

indicators.note: the airline goes within the jumbled letters
upset means overturned, so the state's letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: BA is British Airways

explanation.surface: An aircraft operator in the American state of Idaho annoys a holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Obadiah is a minor Old Testament seer whose book is the shortest in the Hebrew Bible.

clue.text: Revolting peasant with rather common transport sums up life north of here to some capital-dwellers?

definitions.text: sums up life north of here to some capital-dwellers?

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381
a Ford is an ordinary, mass-market car

explanation.surface: An unwashed rustic in a cheap car, set against London snobs' view of the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of Watford' is a London expression for the provinces; Watford is a town just outside London, and 'revolting' means rebelling, not disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Snobbish Londoners dismiss everywhere beyond this nearby town as the uncivilised north, so it marks that boundary.

clue.text: Republican party leader and NI Secretary, ditching Loyalists' leader — boy! getting buzz from party political shenanigans

parts.note: Gerry Adams led Sinn Féin, the Irish republican party

indicators.note: to ditch is to throw away, so these letters are dropped from the name

parts.note: Peter Mandelson was Northern Ireland Secretary from 1999 to 2001

indicators.note: a leader is a first letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word is taken, as its leader
a son is a boy
to give someone a ring or a buzz is to telephone them

explanation.surface: Two Northern Ireland politicians caught up in sectarian intrigue and party games.
explanation.walkthrough: Loyalists are the pro-British side in Northern Ireland. The surname loses its Loyalists' initial and the boy at its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerrymandering is manipulating electoral boundaries for party advantage, an underhand political trick.
